title: Microbundle margin cheatsheet
content:
Purpose:
Quick single-sheet to sanity-check per-bundle economics for a 1k-token microbundle (prepaid small bundle sold in UI). Designed for fast iteration, not final pricing.

Assumptions (baseline) — keep these explicit so we can vary them:
- Infra cost: $3.50 per GPU-hour (blended hosted infra cost; includes networking & misc).
- Effective serving throughput: 300 tokens/sec per GPU (blended across model variants/seq lengths after batching).
- Tokens per GPU-hour = 300 * 3600 = 1,080,000 tokens/hour.
- Infra cost per 1k tokens = 3.50 / 1080 ≈ $0.00324 per 1k tokens.
- OSS model infra ops overhead + SRE amortization: add 10% to infra unit cost → $0.00356 per 1k tokens.
- Customer-facing margin target: 60% gross margin on token units.
- UX friction/marketing & payment fees (relevant to microbundles): ~8% of revenue.

Derived numbers (baseline):
- Baseline cost per 1k tokens (all-in infra+ops): $0.00356.
- To hit 60% gross margin, price per 1k must be: cost / (1 - 0.6) = 0.00356 / 0.4 = $0.0089 → round to $0.009 per 1k tokens.
- So a 1k-token microbundle priced at $0.009 has ~60% gross margin before payment fees. After payment fees (-8% revenue), effective margin drops to ~55%.

Bundle framing examples:
- Microbundle (1k tokens): price $0.009 -> effective cost to us $0.00356 → unit gross margin ≈ 60% (pre-fees).
- Starter pack (10 x 1k): price $0.08 (8c) -> 11% volume discount over single bundle -> blended margin still >55% assuming same cost curve.

Cache & batching sensitivity (important because small interactive apps can be cache-heavy):
- No cache (0% cache hits): cost per 1k = $0.00356 → price @ $0.009 → margin 60%.
- Moderate cache (30% prefix hits): effective tokens served = 0.7 * tokens ⇒ cost per 1k delivered ≈ 0.00356 * 0.7 = $0.00249 → price margin widens, price could be reduced or margin increased.
- High cache (60% hits): cost per 1k ≈ $0.00142 → huge uplift in margin if pricing unchanged.

Short session example — UX math (how many microbundles consumed per session):
- Typical micro UX: 3 prompts + 1 long completion (avg 800 tokens) + 3 short replies (avg 40 tokens each) = 800 + 120 = 920 tokens ~ ~1 microbundle per session.
- If app sends system + 3 messages with prefix reuse, effective token consumption often <1k. That means most users will buy 1 microbundle and not exhaust it for several sessions (good for retention but complicates ARPU calc).

Pay-as-you-go vs bundle economics (seller POV):
- PAYG list price equivalent: if per-1k token PAYG priced at $0.012, microbundle at $0.009 is ~25% off — incentivizes prepayment.
- Psychological pricing: 1k token at $0.009 -> $0.009 is a tiny anchor; show package prices in $ (eg. $0.09 for 10k) to keep mental math simpler.

Commitment & reserve signal (how microbundles map to Dedicated):
- If a customer signals heavy microbundle use > X/month, trigger Nudge for Dedicated / reserved plan. Use usage thresholds (e.g., >500k tokens/month) to recommend commit.

Margin levers to monitor (operational):
- Model mix shift (small -> big models): effective throughput drops → cost per token rises. Monitor per-model throughput and weight into unit econ.
- Quantization improvements: can drop effective token compute by 15–30% for certain models; treat as transitory margin boost.
- Cache hit rate improvements via prefix caching or conversation-level KV cache: low-effort win.
- Burst capacity (bursting to on-demand GPUs): can blow up marginal cost for short periods; need per-account throttles or higher priced burst credits.

Small scenarios (quick sims):
1) Baseline (no cache), price 0.009 -> gross margin ≈ 60% (pre-fees).
2) Moderate cache (30%) with same price -> effective margin ≈ 72%.
3) Model shift to heavier variant (throughput = 150 t/s instead of 300) -> infra cost per 1k doubles -> cost per 1k ≈ $0.00712 -> margin at price 0.009 ≈ 21% (danger zone).

Policy takeaways / heuristics:
- Keep microbundle price low single-digit cents per 1k but with clear nudges to buy larger packs (volume discounts) to improve ARPU.
- Add model-selection surcharge: let users pick cheaper model for microbundle redemption or auto-route by cost-class (saves margin).
- If a customer redeems many bundles and hits sustained heavy usage, upsell to a commitment/reserved conversation flow with discounted per-1k but better predictability (for both sides).
- Track per-customer model mix, cache-hit rate, and 30-day token velocity — use those signals for automated SKU nudges.

UX/Implementation notes:
- Show bundle remaining tokens prominently (low friction redemption).
- Show estimated sessions remaining (derive from typical app session size) — helps reduce surprising spend and supports retention.
- Allow auto-topup with small frictionless checkout and option to opt into monthly starter pack.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Re-run baseline with more realistic blended GPU cost by region (NA vs EU vs APAC).
- Add payroll and sales CAC allocation for microbundle marketing (we currently only include infra+ops).
- Validate typical session token distribution by product vertical (chatbots vs assistants vs search). Owen: can you pull 90-day histogram?
- Consider offering model-level microbundle SKUs (e.g., 1k for cheap-model vs 1k for high-quality-model) — UX complexity tradeoff.

Rough actionables (next 2 weeks):
- Build a tiny sim spreadsheet that parameterizes: gpu_cost, throughput, cache_rate, payment_fee, price_per_1k and outputs margin and threshold for Dedicated upsell.
- Wire a one-line banner in checkout that recommends Starter pack at 10x microbundle price with 10–15% discount.
- Instrument per-user (cohort) cache-hit measurement.

Notes-to-self: keep bundle price in the $0.005–$0.02 per 1k window depending on product-class; well below PAYG to make prepay attractive, but ensure we guard against model mix flips (monitor daily).

End.
